content: Multivitamins are prescribed because vitamins are essential natural substances that your body requires for proper growth, development, and normal functioning. These vitamins are typically obtained from food, and a well-balanced diet usually provides all the necessary vitamins. However, there are specific situations, such as during pregnancy and childhood, when the body’s demand for vitamins increases. Additionally, certain illnesses may impair the body’s ability to obtain or efficiently utilize the vitamins it needs. Multivitamins are therefore prescribed for individuals who require additional vitamins, cannot consume enough food to meet their vitamin needs, or cannot fully benefit from the vitamins present in their diet. In some cases, multivitamins may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Multivitamins are available in various forms, including regular tablets, chewable tablets, capsules, and oral liquids. They are typically taken once daily. It is important to carefully follow the instructions on your prescription or package label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take multivitamins exactly as directed. If your vitamins are in a dropper bottle, use the specially marked dropper to measure each dose accurately. Your doctor will advise you if you need a specific type of vitamin product and the appropriate dosage. Some multivitamin preparations are available without a prescription. Consult your pharmacist for guidance in selecting a suitable multivitamin product and follow the label instructions carefully. Before taking multivitamins, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to multivitamins or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially anticoagulants (commonly referred to as blood thinners) such as warfarin (Coumadin) and any other vitamin supplements. Multivitamins are available in high-dose formulations (therapeutic multivitamins) and in combination with iron, calcium, and other minerals. Do not take these formulations without consulting your doctor. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking multivitamins, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Multivitamins may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: upset stomach or an unpleasant taste. Store this medication in the container it came in, ensuring it is tightly closed and kept out of reach of children. Store it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any medication that is outdated or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call local emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have any questions about multivitamins, consult your pharmacist.
